decisions.reason: The decision changes only the interboard power connector pin order; the I2C cable, clock, pull-up resistance, and pull-up location remain unchanged.
Permission to choose the power connector's electrical pin order does not change the board dimensions, orientation, connector placement, gaps, or mounting-hole constraints.
The charge-status indicator, GPIO assignment, and separate-LED policy are independent of the power connector pin order.
The source concerns the separate interboard power connector, not the J_BAT connector's placement, orientation, family, pin count, or pin functions.
Changing the physical order of signals on the interboard power connector does not alter boost enable control, its pull-down, or the switched 5V load behavior.
The connector pin-order policy does not change any battery protection mode or cutoff value.
The source refers to the interboard power connector rather than the USB-C connector or its sourceability constraints.
Layout-driven selection of connector pin order does not change the required eight-layer board stack.
The battery NTC connection through J_BAT is unaffected by the separate interboard power connector pin order.
The source decision does not alter the requirement for TVS-based ESD protection.
Choosing a signal order that suits the layout does not change component availability, fallback sourcing, or assembled-order availability requirements.
